Respiratory rate is an early warning sign for respiratory failure, sepsis, metabolic disturbance, and deterioration.
Low oxygen saturation directly signals respiratory compromise and can justify urgent treatment.
Temperature helps identify infection, sepsis risk, heat illness, and other risky presentations.
Age changes baseline risk because older adults and very young patients can deteriorate with less obvious symptoms.
Ambulance or helicopter arrival can act as a proxy for pre-hospital severity and urgency.
Chest pain can represent myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, or other time-sensitive diagnoses.
Shortness of breath is tied to hypoxia, heart failure, pneumonia, asthma, COPD, and other urgent conditions.
Altered mental status can signal stroke, sepsis, hypoglycaemia, intoxication, trauma, or neurological emergency.
